Needs changes before merge. One blocking finding remains.

## Requested before merge

1. **P3: Keep the pocket refusal when the area is a closed pocket.** [crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs:80](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/85646344ba1126c1855697a3dcb9aa032ef8a66a/crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs#L80)

   `StockBandRefusal::of` accepts a stock source whenever kept parts exist. The checks in `name` prove that the cutter cannot fit. They do not prove that the area surrounds a part.

   I reproduced this with the existing `block_with_pocket` fixture in a temporary harness outside the checkout:

   - Part: 25.4 × 25.4 × 1.27 mm.
   - Closed pocket: 2 × 20 mm, with its floor at Z 0.1 mm.
   - Box stock: 25.4 × 25.4 × 1.27 mm at the default location. The stock and part have the same outside outline.
   - Operation: 2D Adaptive, stock source, 3 mm tool, Top Z 1.27 mm, Bottom Z 0.1 mm.

   The area contains only the closed pocket. There is no outside stock band. The new code returns:

   ```text
   invalid machining parameters: the stock band around the part is narrower than the tool (3.000 mm diameter, 0.000 mm stock to leave per wall): no cutter position fits. Use a smaller tool or a wider stock margin, or cut the outside with a 2D Contour.
   ```

   The message names the wrong area and gives outside-contour advice for an internal pocket. This also breaks the PR's stated promise to keep true-pocket refusals unchanged.

   Check that the controlled area surrounds kept material before you use the band message. Keep the pocket message for a closed-pocket area. Add a control test with the stock as its source. The added pocket control uses a part selection, so it cannot detect this case.

## What passed

The reported 2 mm outside band still refuses with the 3 mm tool. All eight `narrow_band` tests passed. The tests cover leave, boundary offset, display units, and the curved-band fallback.

I read all three changed files and the current upstream `AGENTS.md`. The trial merge was clean.

## Finding 1: keep the pocket refusal when the area is a closed pocket

**What changed.** `StockBandRefusal::name` now calls `surrounds_kept_material` before it writes the band message.
The rule is for the whole class, not for the one case.
A piece of the stock-minus-part region is a band only when these two conditions are true:

- Its outer loop is a loop of the stock outline.
- Material stands inside that loop.

A closed pocket fails the first condition, because part walls are its boundary.
A pocket around an island also fails the first condition, although it has kept material inside.
These areas keep `pocket is narrower than the tool`.
The stock outline is the same projection that built the region.

**Pins.**

- `a_stock_source_closed_pocket_keeps_its_own_refusal`: your reproduction. The part and the box stock are 25.4 × 25.4 × 1.27 mm. The pocket is 2 × 20 mm. The source is the stock.
- `a_stock_source_pocket_around_an_island_keeps_its_own_refusal`: a 6 × 20 mm pocket with a boss in it, with the stock as the source.

**Mutation proof.**

- Guard disabled: the two new tests failed. The other eight tests passed.
- Only the stock-outline condition disabled: the island test failed. The other nine tests passed.
- Fix restored: all ten `narrow_band` tests passed.

**One behaviour to know.** A strip of stock beside a part that is flush with the other stock sides has no kept material inside it. It keeps the pocket refusal. The decision file records this.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. This is the required Opus safety-tier review of head `0d316a6dc`. No blocking findings.

## Earlier findings

The latest earlier review on this head was clean. The finding of the review on `85646344b` is fixed:

1. **Fixed: keep the pocket refusal for a closed pocket on a stock source.** Commit `0d316a6dc` adds `surrounds_kept_material` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs:142`). Two new controls pin it: `a_stock_source_closed_pocket_keeps_its_own_refusal` and `a_stock_source_pocket_around_an_island_keeps_its_own_refusal`. My mutation A (below) makes the two controls fail.

## Safety reading

I read the full three-file diff. I also read these functions outside the diff: `GenError::map_msg`, `material_of`, `stock_pocket` and `name_outside_entry_refusal`.

- The change only rewrites the text of an error. `GenError::map_msg` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/gen_error.rs:160`) keeps the error kind, the spot and the ghost. A job that refused before still refuses. A job that made a path before makes the same path. The `Ok` branch is not touched.
- The rewrite starts only on the exact text `pocket is narrower than the tool`, for a stock source with kept parts, and for Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset.
- The frame is correct. For `SrcRef::Stock`, `job.material` holds the stock facets in world coordinates (`material.rs:73`). `StockBandRefusal::of` maps them through `local_facets`, the same way `stock_pocket` builds the region (`area.rs:226`). The outline uses the same `slice::project(.., FOOTPRINT_SAMPLES)`.
- The diff adds no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. Each failed geometry step keeps the generator's own message.
- The diff does not change posted G-code, gouge or collision checks, stock simulation or geometry output. I still ran two mutations because this is the safety-tier review.

## Mutations (local, in the review worktree, then restored)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| A: guard off (`if false && !surrounds_kept_material(..)`) | RED: `a_stock_source_closed_pocket_keeps_its_own_refusal`, `a_stock_source_pocket_around_an_island_keeps_its_own_refusal` |
| B: band rewrite off (`if true \|\| ..`, the generator text always stays) | RED: the five band pins (`..names_the_band_width_and_a_fix`, `..names_stock_to_leave`, `..measures_the_controlled_boundary`, `..uses_document_inches`, `..curved_stock_band..`) |
| File restored | GREEN: all ten `narrow_band` tests |

## Optional, non-blocking

1. `StockBandRefusal::of` (`run_job.rs:82`) clones the region and the stock facets for each stock-source pocket-family job, also when the job succeeds. A mesh stock can have many facets. A follow-up can keep only references, or build the context only on the error path. Suggested level: `P7`.
2. With Outside containment on a stock source, `name_outside_entry_refusal` (`run_job.rs:210`) can add its own advice after the new sentence, because the new text still contains "narrower than the tool". The result is two pieces of advice in one message. It is not wrong. A follow-up can check this case. Suggested level: `P7`.
